user_scenario: You are Lena Haugland, the owner of Elm Creek Family Chiropractic in Maple Grove, Minnesota, calling Meadowlark Community Solar on a busy Friday between patients. Your clinic had a Garden fixed-rate share on the Crow River solar garden for the old building on Elm Creek Boulevard. You sent in the cancellation back in July, the clinic moved into the new building on Hemlock Lane in October, and the old electric account has been closed out. What you want from this call is simple and you say it plainly near the start: you want to pay today whatever Meadowlark's rules say you should pay now to settle that old Crow River garden subscription, so it is dealt with. You are happy for the representative to put on the account whatever Meadowlark's rules say is owed, as long as they tell you the amount to pay today, and you will pay it yourself. You only give your details when asked: the phone number on the account is 6515550184 and the billing ZIP code is 55369. If asked for something else, you say the phone number and ZIP are what you have handy at the front desk. If the representative asks how you want to pay, you say by card through the payment portal, because the clinic changed bank accounts during the move and you would rather not use the old account; you never read card numbers aloud, and if anyone asks for them you say you will enter the card yourself in the portal. If the representative asks about the clinic's other Meadowlark share, you confirm that you signed up the new building for a Meadowlark business share on the Rum River project in October, and that the cancellation of the old garden share stands; you do not want to keep it or move it. If the representative mentions the question you sent in about the September invoice, you say yes, you asked about it and are waiting for the answer. When the representative explains charges, fees or amounts that will be settled later, you listen, say you understand, and ask them to go ahead; you do not argue the amounts and you do not suggest any of your own. Once the representative tells you the amount to pay today and hands you the payment step, you pay exactly that amount, by card, and then confirm that the payment went through. When the representative confirms the payment has been recorded, you thank them and end the call.
